science.headline: How some COVID vaccines triggered rare blood-clot disorder
science.teaser: Nature, Published online: 12 February 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-00457-4 Researchers identify genetic mutation in small group of people who developed the serious disorder after receiving the AstraZeneca or Johnson & Johnson vaccine.
science.tldr: Reveals potential genetic link between vaccine and rare blood-clot disorder

science.headline: AI agents are hiring human 'meatspace workers' — including some scientists
science.teaser: Nature, Published online: 13 February 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-00454-7 Biologists, physicists and computer scientists have joined a platform called RentAHuman.ai to advertise their skills.
science.tldr: Discoveries challenge traditional roles and skills in academia with AI hiring

science.headline: RFK Jr. follows a carnivore diet. That doesn’t mean you should.
science.teaser: Americans have a new set of diet guidelines. Robert F. Kennedy Jr. has taken an old-fashioned food pyramid, turned it upside down, and plonked a steak and a stick of butter in prime positions. Kennedy and his Make America Healthy Again mates have long been extolling the virtues of meat and whole-fat
science.tldr: Raises concerns about the potential health risks associated with carnivore diets

science.headline: Self-powered vibration sensor for wearable health care and voice detection
science.teaser: Nature, Published online: 12 February 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-00250-3 Densely packed arrays of electrical components called capacitors can form a high-fidelity vibration sensor that can be worn on the skin.
science.tldr: Reveals new physics principles for densely packed capacitor arrays

science.headline: Why EVs are gaining ground in Africa
science.teaser: EVs are getting cheaper and more common all over the world. But the technology still faces major challenges in some markets, including many countries in Africa. Some regions across the continent still have limited grid and charging infrastructure, and those that do have widespread electricity access
science.tldr: Accelerates adoption in Africa as costs decrease

science.headline: Why self-expansion is the key to long-lasting love and friendship
science.teaser: A growing body of psychological research shows that the best relationships – romantic or otherwise – come with a feeling of personal growth. Columnist David Robson explores the evidence-backed ways to broaden our horizons and connect more deeply with our loves, our friends and ourselves
science.tldr: Emphasizes that personal growth is essential for long-lasting love and friendship

science.headline: Accidental discovery hints at mystery structures within our brain
science.teaser: Scientists may have stumbled across a network of vessels in the brain that helps clear out waste fluid – a discovery that could "represent a paradigm shift in our understanding of all neurodegenerative diseases"
science.tldr: Identifies previously unknown network responsible for clearing brain waste fluid

science.headline: Gene editing that spreads within the body could cure more diseases
science.teaser: The idea of self-amplifying gene editing is to get cells to pass on packages of CRISPR machinery to their neighbours, boosting the effect
science.tldr: Unlocks new avenues for treating genetic diseases by spreading gene editing

science.headline: Endurance brain cells may determine how long you can run for
science.teaser: The activity of certain neurons may influence our endurance for exercise, and these could be targeted to help us run faster for longer
science.tldr: Activates potential for improved endurance through targeted brain cell interventions

science.headline: These 5 diets could add years to your life even if you have bad genes
science.teaser: Five dietary patterns that involve eating lots of plants have been linked with living up to three years longer, even among people who are genetically predisposed to have a shorter life
science.tldr: Increases understanding of plant-based diets' potential life-extending effects significantly

science.headline: RNA strand that can almost self-replicate may be key to life's origins
science.teaser: Life may have begun when RNA molecules began to replicate themselves, and now we’ve finally found an RNA molecule that is very close to being able to do this
science.tldr: Reveals a possible mechanism for life's emergence in RNA molecules

science.headline: CAR T-cell therapy may slow neurodegenerative conditions like ALS
science.teaser: Immune cells in the brain that go rogue contribute to the death of neurons, so getting rid of them may slow the progression of neurodegenerative conditions like amyotrophic lateral sclerosis
science.tldr: Could upend our understanding of neurodegenerative diseases and their treatments

science.headline: Exploring sci-fi treats from George Saunders and Matthew Kressel
science.teaser: In George Saunders's Vigil, a ghost visits Earth to help a dying oil tycoon, while terraforming efforts on Mars are about to bear fruit in The Rainseekers by Matthew Kressel. Emily H. Wilson's sci-fi column explores two very different short novels
science.tldr: Challenges conventional perceptions with thought-provoking sci-fi themes

science.headline: World’s oldest cold virus found in 18th-century woman's lungs
science.teaser: Finding rhinoviruses, which cause the common cold, in preserved medical specimens and analysing their RNA genome could let us trace the evolution of human illness
science.tldr: Analyzing virus evolution helps scientists better understand human health history

science.headline: Huge hot blobs inside Earth may have made its magnetic field wonky
science.teaser: Simulations suggest that two enormous masses of hot rock have been involved in generating Earth’s magnetic field and giving it an irregular shape
science.tldr: Overturns long-held understanding of Earth's magnetic field generation mechanisms

society.headline: In Whitechapel, a new England struggles to be born
society.teaser: A dispatch from the knife-edge of the nation's multiculturalism debate
society.tldr: Highlights the ongoing struggle for England's multicultural identity in Whitechapel

society.headline: Losing Faith in Atheism
society.teaser: I spent years searching for a livable secular world view, but none of them quite offered the value of belief.
society.tldr: Reconciles the search for meaning in a secular world view

society.headline: “Love Story” Is a Forgettable Elegy for Gen X
society.teaser: The FX series, with its Wikipedia-page-like narrowness on the romance between John F. Kennedy, Jr., and Carolyn Bessette, excises all that contemporary drama that makes the Kennedy story, one of a relationship to a greater culture, so compelling.
society.tldr: Challenges conventional portrayals of the Kennedy marriage in popular media

society.headline: The Disappearance of Nancy Guthrie
society.teaser: The search for the “Today” show host’s mother, nearing its second week, has transfixed the public in Arizona and beyond.
society.tldr: Searchers are actively searching for Nancy Guthrie, the missing woman

society.headline: Anneliese Dodds: “I felt Peter Mandelson was a clear blackmail risk”
society.teaser: The former shadow chancellor on the Mandelson Affair, foreign aid and countering the tech bros
society.tldr: Raises concerns about Labour's handling of allegations against its former leader

society.headline: Kristi Noem’s Audience of One
society.teaser: The DHS secretary is suddenly talking about more than just mass deportations.
society.tldr: Reveals surprising nuances in Kristi Noem's policy stance on immigration

society.headline: A Tour Through Central Park’s Cruising Grounds
society.teaser: Arthur Tress’s new book, “The Ramble, NYC 1969,” provides a view into a world otherwise all but invisible to passersby.
society.tldr: Reveals a hidden world beneath the surface of everyday urban life

society.headline: The Clash of Civilizations Was an Inside Job
society.teaser: After 9/11, Samuel P. Huntington’s big idea was everywhere. But he missed the coming war within.
society.tldr: Reveals the overlooked internal conflict within Huntington's theory on 9/11

society.headline: The Worst Years of Our Life
society.teaser: Where will the rise of Trump and Minneapolis martyrs take us? The post The Worst Years of Our Life appeared first on Harper's Magazine .
society.tldr: Destabilizes our understanding of politics and social justice with alarming consequences

society.headline: Weekly Review
society.teaser: The figure skater Ilia Malinin landed the first legal one-legged backflip in a competition since 1976. The post Weekly Review appeared first on Harper's Magazine .
society.tldr: Upends centuries-old records with Ilia Malinin's record-breaking one-legged backflip

society.headline: The Fine Balance Required of an ‘Authorial Rant’
society.teaser: A cherished grudge might make it into a novel—but the best writers avoid creating books that feel one-sided.
society.tldr: Overturns outdated notions about authorial rants and their impact on readers

society.headline: The Most Sought-After Head of Government in Europe
society.teaser: Few know Jens-Frederik Nielsen, but everyone wants to talk to him.
society.tldr: Reveals Jens-Frederik Nielsen's leadership as highly sought-after in Europe

society.headline: Consuming the Empire
society.teaser: Sugar, tea, and tobacco tied British daily life to empire, turning global exploitation into ordinary habits of consumption. The post Consuming the Empire appeared first on JSTOR Daily .
society.tldr: Challenges prevailing narratives about consumerism and empire's ordinary effects

society.headline: Why Europe Is Talking About Nukes
society.teaser: Declining confidence in America means deepening discussions of collective European deterrence.
society.tldr: Raises questions about Europe's military independence from the US

society.headline: Dorothy Parker: Sharp-Witted Writer, Bitter Professor
society.teaser: Dorothy Parker’s year as a visiting professor shows how a celebrated literary voice struggled to adapt to the realities of academic teaching. The post Dorothy Parker: Sharp-Witted Writer, Bitter Professor appeared first on JSTOR Daily .
society.tldr: Reveals the challenges faced by famous writers in academia
